items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: when I lived next door to Lynn's.

ctx.x: Let me ask you this, Papa. Do you recall, when was it when you heard your first rag? When did you hear the first rag you ever heard in your life? First rag I ever heard in my life? Yeah.

Were you a little baby or a kid or? Oh, no. No, no. I was around the time when I used to play around with the kids around about, well, when I lived next door to Lynn's. That's before we were, long before we were married. I must have been about eight years old. Eight years old?

I must have been about eight years old. That would have been about 1881? Seven like that. Seven like that. You don't remember the name of the first rag. I don't guess you would. No, I don't. What about cakewalks? Ask him if you heard any cakewalks. How about cakewalks? You hear many cakewalks. No, we used to play it, but then it was out before I played it. I see. It was out before you were able to play? Yeah. No. Ask him. No, we were playing music. What do you mean out? If it was out of style? No, no. If it was…
